title: Prepositions of Time: In, On, At
summary: Learn how to use 'in', 'on', and 'at' correctly with times and dates. Talk about your daily schedule and favorite days with confidence.

sections.p: We use the word 'at' when we talk about a specific clock time. For example, when you want to say what time you wake up, eat lunch, or start work. It helps you be very exact about your schedule during the day.

ex.en: The class starts at half past nine.
ex.mean: The exact time the lesson begins.

sections.h: Use ON for days and dates
sections.p: We use the word 'on' for days of the week, like Monday or Saturday. We also use 'on' when we talk about a specific calendar date, such as your birthday or a holiday with a date.

ex.en: I have a test on Monday.
ex.mean: A specific day of the week.

sections.h: Use IN for months, years, and long times
sections.p: We use the word 'in' for longer periods of time. This includes months, years, seasons, and general parts of the day like the morning or the afternoon. Think of 'in' as being inside a bigger box of time.

ex.en: I drink coffee in the morning.

tip: Think of 'at' as a tiny dot on a clock, 'on' as a page in a calendar, and 'in' as a big box of time!

quiz.en: We go to the beach ___ summer.
